description: Resolver expectations (A2.1e, D71), fixed before any resolver code existed. R01-R36 are the brief's section 12.2 cases; V, B and M cases are section 12.3; P cases are provenance on accepted fixtures. Hand-worked arithmetic is in each note. Each case gets its own scene ID fixture.resolver.<id>, command fx.<id>.command and query fx.<id>.query, so no evidence-changing variant shares a geometry-cache key. See README.md for the variant operations and expectation keys.

an answer field in a node

a wrong arity: between with one anchor
a wrong arity: user_heading with an anchor
a label with a trailing newline, which Python's $ would let through
a rank anchored on its own node
between naming one anchor node twice
a QUERY with a null action
a matching map with an unmapped label

two copies of the scene's map
a command for another scene ID
an identical second reading reuses every predicate

another frame never aliases. By hand, user at (-2,-2): anchor obj_001, v=(2,2)/sqrt8, right=(1,-1)/sqrt2; obj_003 (1,2): -0.707 F, obj_004 (-1,2): -2.121 F -> no_match. Anchor obj_002, v=(2,6)/sqrt40, right=(0.9487,-0.3162); obj_003 (1,-2): 1.581 T, obj_004 (-1,-2): -0.316 F -> resolved obj_003
an identical rank reuses its entry; k=2 is a new key. By hand, k=2 with D={005}, P={006}: subset {} gives no_match, {006} gives obj_006 -> insufficient
trace on/off and small trace caps
an ambiguous branch plus a missing-evidence reading is insufficient
